To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the k-nearest neighbor outlier methods have different performance profiles on different datasets; (ii) there are datasets that are more suitable than others as benchmark sets for outlier detection; (iii) the performance of the methods depends strongly on the choice of parameter values, and (iv) the commonly-used measures are not suitable for evaluating outlier detection results, but can be modified to provide a more accurate picture of the performance of different outlier detection algorithms.

(a) the most appropriate measures to evaluate outlier detection results are the area under ROC curve, the F-measure, and the average precision measure, (b) the LOF and LOCI methods are the top performers across the majority of the datasets, and (c) the most appropriate benchmark sets for outlier detection are the KDDCup99, the MNIST, and the COIL-20 datasets.

(1) the LOF algorithm outperforms all other methods on most datasets, and is the only method that performs consistently well; (2) the performance of outlier detection methods is highly sensitive to parameter choices; and (3) there is little evidence that the commonly-used outlier detection evaluation measures are suitable for the task.
